svg.title: TOPAK D2 — Policy composition: admit ⟺ floor_permit ∧ ¬bundle_deny
svg.desc: Two tiers decide every admit over one frozen input. The floor, a verified evaluator linked into the mechanism, is the only tier that can permit. The bundle, per-request and signed, is asked only whether to refuse, and only after the floor permits, and only from a bundle that loaded signed and well-formed. Composition is a mechanism constant, so bundle ⊑ floor holds for every bundle at every age; what it cannot bound, delivery over labels, the floor bounds with a minimum no bundle can loosen. An operator's control request is decided by the floor alone.
svg.text: TOPAK · D2

Two tiers decide every admit over one frozen input. The floor, a verified evaluator linked into the mechanism, is the only tier that can permit. The bundle, per-request and signed, is asked only whether to refuse, and only after the floor permits, and only from a bundle that loaded signed and well-formed. Composition is a mechanism constant, so bundle ⊑ floor holds for every bundle at every age; what it cannot bound,
delivery over labels, the floor bounds with a minimum no bundle can loosen. An operator's control request is decided by the floor alone.
evaluated by the mechanism over one frozen input (ADR-0030 §1, §4); fail-closed on both sides; a floor deny short-circuits
Principal (the seat), action, resource, context and the
complete entity slice, in schema S's shape, plus the
bundle's view built from the same facts (FrozenInput,
lift.rs).
Resolved once. Floor and bundle read the same facts; the
bundle may not re-fetch anything about the request. Its own
shipped data is not a re-fetch (ADR-0030 §4 R1).
Written only by the typed lift and the issued rules: no bundle
has a write path to any value the floor reads (§3).
Context: epoch, fence, rules epoch, round, round role, lease
fields; for Run observerLive and the label facts clearSet,
inputLabels, destLiteral, destLabels, with
Tool.outward (ADR-0030 A2); for a control action
ControlCtx, thirteen facts the mechanism holds (ADR-0050
§4); erasureQuorum for Erase.
The label facts are computed from the record and the granted
revision's allowlist entry: the lift's work, not a re-fetch, and
both tiers see the same values (ADR-0030 A2).
Its digest is recorded in the admit.

text.tspan: Floor tier · Cedar, linked · the only tier that can permit

svg.text: Obligation (§2): an evaluator with a mechanized semantics; an implementation checked against it; a decidable comparison of two policy sets over a declared
schema (implies, equivalent, always-allows, always-denies, never-errors); resident and linked; minimal. Cedar meets it; the reference links cedar-policy 4.13,
the Rust engine, the shorter chain to the Lean model (§3).
A library, not a service: no process, no socket, no fetch. Text, schema S and values file compiled in by path; the replica refuses to start unless their bytes
match the gated digests (ADR-0033 §2): since 9c57221 the emergency stage's, 15c941b9… and d3c8145c… (A12).
Schema S enforced on every request: a non-conforming input is a deny. S changes only with a mechanism release (§4).
Any evaluation error is a deny: Cedar skips a policy that errors, so a skipped forbid would let a permit through.
A deny names its reason: the forbids that fired, or FloorNoPermit when none did (finding 10).
Evaluation: any satisfied forbid denies; else any satisfied permit allows; else deny.

Built from the genesis draft (17 policies) in three gated stages, labels, control, emergency (diagram B8). Genesis-provisional: gated, pinned and enforced, and ratified
only when the bootstrap reviewer establishes that it is fit, with no test (ADR-0029 A4; G10 item 87). Not in the floor, and why (file header): epoch fencing and the round
bound are the mechanism's; the rules floor bounds issuances, not admits (§7); Invoke hermeticity is an obligation on each allowlist entry; F4 to F6 are load checks (right).
Values file (ADR-0039 §1): T_obs, K, T_persona, the unset θ, every number a placeholder.

text.tspan: Bundle tier · OPA/Rego sidecar, WASM fallback · can only refuse

svg.text: Obligation (§2): signed; evaluated per request over syntactically lifted input; the three ADR-0007 gates. Any per-request engine
discharges it, because the mechanism does the composition.
Consulted only after a floor permit, and asked only whether to refuse: the mechanism reads data.topak.bundle.allow, and
allow if not refused.
Counts only from the revision the lease names (ADR-0031 §1 bundle); a renewal keeps the bundle.
Loads only under a signature over its content revision that verifies under a key in the issued rules' bundle_keys (ADR-0044
§1–§3); implemented at the reference by ADR-0033 A6 (Batch 23). A sidecar's answer counts only from a verified revision; a grant
naming an unverified one is refused.
Loads only if its allowlist is well-formed: W1 to W10 (ADR-0049 §6), checked by the mechanism after the signature and before
any decision counts. A mechanism constant, as composition is; a bundle cannot waive them (ADR-0030 A2). Table below.
Today the key is a throwaway dev key with custody (1, 0); signing at promotion is a script step, since no promotion pipeline exists
(item 67, open).
Not consulted for a control request: at the reference an operator's request is decided by the floor's C1 to C9 alone (ADR-0033

Checked by the mechanism after the signature and before any decision counts; a mechanism constant no bundle can waive (ADR-0030 A2).
"Outward" is derived, never declared: W7 and W9 read the targets the issued rules list as inside the deployment, and W8 the entries they
name as allowed to release a reserved name (ADR-0025 A2; ADR-0030 A2). The rules' well-formedness reads both, and the rules floor
bounds neither (ADR-0033 A15). Read once, from the genesis rules, when bundles load: an issuance that changes a list does not re-check a
bundle already loaded (I46; G10 item 94).

mechanism checks of D1 step 3 run first.
The composition is one decision: the floor and bundle are not

text.tspan: What the floor bounds that composition cannot, and what reaches the floor alone (Batch 34)
A minimum over labels that no bundle can loosen

svg.text: Run's ingress is four items, each with a label (ADR-0043 A1): the task, consulted content, tool results and the tool list. An item is delivered clear with its label, or as a handle with no bytes, by a delivery table in bundle data, per
seat kind (ADR-0047 §2).
Delivery is not bounded by bundle ⊑ floor, which is decided over action variants. A promoted bundle may move every label to clear (ADR-0047 §8).

So the floor carries a minimum (ADR-0047 §7; ADR-0041 A1): R5 to R7, forbids over the label facts the lift supplies. They are monotone in clearSet: delivering more in the clear buys a narrower round (G10 §2.5). Relaxing
them is an issuance with the floor's gates.
A bundle may add rules over clearSet and inputLabels, and can only narrow (ADR-0041 §5).

At the reference: the label facts are the deciding replica's and apply re-checks only clearSet (G10 item 93); a person on an emergency seat is given handles unless the bundle says otherwise, since the load check asks for no
delivery row for that kind (G10 §3, result 6; item 92).

text.tspan: An operator's request: the floor alone

svg.text: Six control actions of an operator seat (ADR-0050 §4): Regrant, Renew, AttestGates add and need a live lease and a live peer; EndRound, Revoke, FenceEpoch deny and need no lease, except the fleet fence; a lapsed
operator denies on a fresh sign-on assertion.
Signed with the seat's key, with the fleet epoch and a counter. The deciding replica computes thirteen facts into ControlCtx; the operator supplies none (ADR-0033 A11).

C1 to C9 decide, and there is no bundle tier: admit ⟺ floor_permit for these actions at the reference. Every replica verifies the signature, refuses a replayed counter, recomputes the facts and refuses the entry if they differ, and
restates the envelope before applying (control.rs).
The envelope is stated twice, in Cedar and in Rust, and only the tests hold them together (A11).
BOOTSTRAP: the unsigned socket is kept and seats, and does nothing else; a first lease from a completed tally is not built (ADR-0050 §10; G10 item 88).

bundle ⊑ floor survives D-0030-1: composition is a mechanism constant and does not depend on the floor's language. The reference declares neither degeneracy since 2026.10.01 (ADR-0030 A1, Batch 24).

bundle ⊑ floor for every bundle, at every age, of the composed decision. It is no longer something a bundle can fail; a bundle whose text permits more than the floor is inert, not inadmissible. Refinement is still
discharged at promotion, now by construction.
Containment is checked against the floor, and no bundle can weaken it.
Stale bundles are monotone-safe, with no refinement premise: local enforcement under partition survives, sound by construction (the same shape as the lease argument).
No cross-language check. Deciding refinement with an SMT solver over Rego needed a mechanized Rego semantics that does not exist; composition removes the need.
Floor tightening never invalidates a promoted bundle.
A bundle cannot establish that something is allowed: always_allows over the composed decision is not provable.
Over-denial by a bundle is a modeled, attributed local event (deny=all is F2, ADR-0028).

A bundle can narrow a floor exception (§5) and the emergency seat's calls, which R1 admits like any other: a bad bundle can disable an emergency seat's tools, a liveness cost, never a widening (ToO rev 14 §3.1).
bundle ⊑ floor says nothing about delivery: it is decided over action variants. A promoted bundle may move every label to clear; only the floor's R5 to R7 bound that (ADR-0047 §8).
Two languages and two engines; the floor must fit PARC: no aggregation, no regex, no computed data.

Neither Rego → Cedar nor Cedar → Rego is in the archetype. A transpiler is a Build artifact whose output becomes the enforced floor, and Build is where the Byzantine threat lives: a silent mistranslation means the
proven text is not the enforced text.
Cedar's analyses compare Cedar with Cedar. A deployment that keeps a Rego floor declares D-0030-1.

text.tspan: The truth table's first two groups, proved of the code (ADR-0053, Proposed)

svg.text: mechanism/lean/Topak/Admit.lean transcribes floor_gate and compose from admit.rs, and the call site in mechanism.rs, and proves of the transcription: admit_iff, that the decision is floor_permit ∧

¬bundle_deny at every floor and bundle outcome; that an admit carries exactly the floor's reasons and the bundle's engine and digest; that a floor error is a deny whatever the bundle said; that every floor deny names a
reason, FloorNoPermit and never an empty Floor([]); and that the node's own gate check before the bundle call is compose.

Of the transcription, read beside the Rust; on the Lean kernel (T-0045-37, proposed). Three mutated transcriptions (M_OVERRIDE, M_ERR, the empty-reason deny) each fail to build. Not a refinement (T-0045-28).

The control-request rows are not covered: there mechanism.rs matches the floor's outcome directly, without floor_gate or compose, and a deny with no forbid fired is returned with its facts and an empty reason list
rather than as FloorNoPermit.

Entities present in every request: Roster::grant, Roster::veto, the requesting Seat with its roster parents, CorpusRoot::pinned and
run-pinned, the Workspace ws-<seat>-e<epoch>-r<round>, ToolSet::build-allow and run-allow; then the action's resource, with
Tool.outward from the label facts, and the context in the shapes above. No bg-tools since the emergency stage.
For a control request (lift_control): the two rosters, the operator's seat, the target seat, artifact or Fleet, and ControlCtx from the facts (51
entities in the stage's test slice, emergency-tests.json).
Erase, EraseCtx and ArchiveRecord are typed, gated and never produced: no lift path exists and Rules.erasure_roster is never read (G11).
Lease.rulesEpoch, Tool.digest and VoteCtx.epoch are typed and lifted and no policy reads them: B6 reads context.rulesEpoch, and a
tool's digest is in its entity id name@digest (inventory finding 23).
Report takes clearSet and no entry reads it yet (ADR-0041 §4, A1).
S is enforced on every request, so an attribute's absence is a deny even where no policy would read it.
